investigations.name: colonies-01-hpc-readiness
investigations.description:
Build phase fixed daughter-process hydration so structural _add instantiates
daughter EcoliWCMs through the engine. Decide-phase N-sweep (N ∈ {1,2,4,8}) on
one machine measured per-tick wall, per-cell cost, peak RSS, and pymunk step,
extrapolated to a cells-per-HPC-node budget, and identified the GIL as the
dominant bottleneck. Output: 384 cells/node at 450 MB/cell (commit 2f950d9);
the 2026-07-27 hardening re-measurement on current main (bounded phenotype
recorder) gives ~291 MB/cell → ~700 cells/node (F-03).
investigations.title: HPC scaling readiness for the colony composite
investigations.objective:
Is the pure whole-cell colony composite ready to scale on HPC? Can N
parallel EcoliWCMs grow and divide cleanly for ≥2 generations inside one
composite, and how does wall-time / RAM / per-tick cost scale with N on one
machine — well enough to project a cells-per-HPC-node budget?

investigations.name: colonies-02-parallel-multigen-perf
investigations.description:
Rerun the colony from one whole-cell agent, dividing naturally (no forced
same-tick division), keeping both daughters, as it doubles 1 → 2 → 4 → 8.
Track the per-cell compute hit (wall, RSS) generation-by-generation to resolve
colonies-01's open F-06 anomaly (RSS climbing ~5 MB/sim-s in long runs) and its
PASS-narrow caveat (only forced division was validated). Run the same growing
colony under the process-bigraph Ray protocol (sharded RayProtocol / actor
pool) to test whether process-level parallelism lifts the single-process
~13-cells GIL ceiling. Produce a compute-requirements profile seeding
colonies-03-hpc-deployment.
investigations.title: Parallel multi-generation colony — natural-division perf & Ray scaling
investigations.objective:
Starting from one whole-cell E. coli agent dividing naturally through 3-4
generations (1 → 2 → 4 → 8), does per-cell compute cost (wall + RSS) stay
flat, or drift as daughter EcoliWCM internal composites accumulate history?
And does running the growing colony under the process-bigraph Ray protocol
(one OS process per cell / sharded actor pool) lift the single-process GIL
ceiling colonies-01 measured (~13 cells/process at realtime)?

investigations.name: colonies-03-wcm-rss-leak
investigations.description:
Part A enabling-infrastructure study. colonies-02 recorded a single EcoliWCM
growing RSS ~7.7 MB/sim-s on the macOS mini, reaching ~19 GB before first
division and OOM-killing the sequential colony at 27.5 GB (~34 GB at 2 Ray
cells) — which read as an unbounded native leak blocking HPC deployment.

The 2026-07-26 leak hunt corrected that framing: the per-tick growth is
LOCALIZED (per-process RSS attribution on the mini) to the inner WCM's
polypeptide-elongation step (~82%) + mass-listener (~17%). It is not
unbounded. The truly-retained part is small (~0.2 MB/tick, tracemalloc-visible:
scipy LSODA integrator work arrays held per solve); the scary ~1.4 MB/tick is
macOS allocator arena retention of elongation's per-tick numpy working arrays,
a macOS measurement artifact. A faithful Linux (glibc) reproduction grows only
0.017 MB/tick WITHOUT any fix and 0.000 MB/tick WITH periodic malloc_trim(0),
versus ~1.6 MB/tick on the macOS mini — so on the Linux HPC target the colony's
memory is BOUNDED. The leak is now a characterised, Linux-bounded, mitigated
footnote, not an HPC blocker.
investigations.title: Inner EcoliWCM RSS leak — localize and fix
investigations.objective:
Where does the RSS growth in a single EcoliWCM come from, and is it bounded
on the Linux HPC target so per-cell RSS budgets are trustworthy? (Answered:
localized to elongation + mass-listener; small real retention is scipy LSODA
work arrays; the rest is macOS arena churn; on Linux/glibc it is bounded.)

investigations.name: colonies-04-device-phenotype-harness
investigations.description:
Part B (phenotype tier) \u2014 build the shared colony-phenotyping harness and
establish the cheapest rung of the cost/fidelity tier ladder (simple viva-munk
agent -> growth surrogate -> full WCM). Stands up the cell-tier factory, the
geometry builders (mother machine, daughter machine, free colony), and the
tier-agnostic phenotype extractor, then validates the measurement pipeline with
cheap simple agents before spending WCM compute.

The extractor recovers the common single-cell phenotype panel \u2014 growth rate,
size-at-division, added length, inter-division time, and the adder
size-homeostasis relation \u2014 streamed per cell to zarr by the
ColonyPhenotypeRecorder (a process that takes a cheap view of the cells map,
not a deep-copying emitter), so the panel is a bounded per-cell stream. The
distributions are held for later comparison across the higher-fidelity tiers
and against experimental microfluidic-device data.
investigations.title: Device harness + simple-agent phenotype baseline
investigations.objective:
Does the shared harness — cell-tier factory, geometry builders, and
tier-agnostic phenotype extractor — recover a correct, uniform single-cell
phenotype panel (growth rate, size-at-division, added length, inter-division
time, adder size-homeostasis) across the three device geometries, validated
first with cheap simple viva-munk agents before spending WCM compute?

investigations.name: colonies-05-mother-machine
investigations.description:
Part B (phenotype tier) \u2014 run the canonical viva-munk MOTHER MACHINE (narrow
dead-end channels with a flow channel that washes out cells crossing the top),
populated by viva-munk's simple grow/divide agents: the cheapest rung of the
cost/fidelity tier ladder (simple agent -> growth surrogate -> full WCM). The
simulation runs now and produces (a) an animated GIF of the device running and
(b) distribution figures for the core emergent single-cell phenotypes \u2014 size
at division, inter-division time (birth to division), added length before
division, and the adder size-homeostasis relation \u2014 extracted uniformly by
colony_bench.phenotypes.

This tier establishes the measurement + visualization pipeline against cheap
agents; the phenotype distributions are held for comparison against the WCM
tier (colonies-09) and experimental mother-machine microfluidic data. No
biological conclusion is drawn at the simple-agent tier.

size-homeostasis relation \u2014 extracted uniformly by colony_bench.phenotypes.

This tier establishes the measurement + visualization pipeline against cheap

investigations.name: colonies-08-wcm-daughter-machine
investigations.description:
Run the REAL v2ecoli whole-cell BASELINE \u2014 the full 55-process EcoliWCM \u2014 as a
single cell inside the daughter-machine device geometry (chamber + absorbing
wall), letting it grow and divide naturally. This is the highest-fidelity rung
of the phenotype ladder (simple viva-munk agent -> growth surrogate -> full
WCM): it asks whether the emergent single-cell phenotypes \u2014 adder
size-homeostasis, size at division, added length before division,
inter-division time, and growth rate \u2014 survive whole-cell colony embedding and
division inside the device. Renders the running animation and the same
phenotype figures as the cheap-agent device studies, so the whole-cell tier can
be compared, in the same geometry and on the identical measurement pipeline,
against the simple viva-munk agents (colonies-06) and against experimental
microfluidic-device data.

A bounded per-cell phenotype panel (size, added length, division/birth times,
growth rate) is streamed to zarr by the ColonyPhenotypeRecorder \u2014 a process,
not an emitter, so recording stays cheap. Memory is characterised and
Linux-bounded, not a blocker: the inner WCM's per-tick RSS growth is localized
to the polypeptide-elongation step + mass-listener and is dominated on the dev
mini by a macOS allocator artifact (~1.6 MB/tick), but is only ~0.017 MB/tick
on glibc and ~0.000 with periodic malloc_trim. WCM-tier runs are therefore
length-capped on the dev mini yet effectively unbounded on the Linux HPC
target. On the mini this run spans only a few generations, so phenotype
distributions are PRELIMINARY (small n); full distributions await the Linux HPC
run and experimental data (colonies-09). The value here is the genuine
whole-cell baseline running inside the device.

investigations.name: genotype-00-build-integrity
investigations.title: Does a ParCa-level knockout reconstruct into a self-consistent sim_data?
investigations.objective: When a gene is deleted from the chromosome and the ParCa is rebuilt on the perturbed genome, does the resulting sim_data stay self-consistent? Concretely: is every retained feature's sequence exactly what it should be, does the feature inventory change by exactly the expected amount, does every coordinate still lie inside the shortened chromosome, and does the fit converge with its parameters in range - before any physiological reading is attempted.

investigations.name: genotype-01-control-panel
investigations.title: What do ParCa-level knockout mechanics look like across control gene classes?
investigations.objective: When genes of three verified classes are knocked out at the ParCa level - (A) expressed but functionally unwired in the model, (B) wired into metabolism but biologically non-essential, (C) essential machinery with three distinct mechanisms (RNA polymerase, ribosome, replisome) - what do the build mechanics actually do? Does every class build? Does the fit converge? How large is the expression perturbation beyond the deleted gene (the refit-artifact floor)? And is anything general or surprising in how the mechanics differ across classes?
investigations.claim: Knockout mechanics are structurally sound and class-independent (8/8 genotypes pass every fit-free integrity axis), but a step-3 dangling-reference crash in set_ppgpp_expression blocks the build for ALL ~393 ppGpp-regulated genes (~8% of the genome) - preempting any in-model essentiality signal - and the refit artifact for inert knockouts is per-mille in the bulk with ~10% shifts confined to the target's operon neighbors.

investigations.name: ketchup-exchange-comparison
investigations.title: v2ecoli baseline central-carbon exchange phenotype vs KETCHUP kinetic models
investigations.objective:
Does the v2ecoli baseline central-carbon exchange / byproduct phenotype
(glucose, O2, CO2, acetate, NH3, SO4) match the KETCHUP core-metabolism
kinetic models k-ecoli74 and k-ecoli307, when both are glucose-normalized and
graded by the report-card flux_scatter criterion?

investigations.name: ko-and-media
investigations.title: Knockout and media perturbations on the baseline whole cell
investigations.objective:
How do a translation-level gene knockout (lacY) and an amino-acid-rich medium
each move the v2ecoli baseline off its wild-type trajectory — and how do you
express each as a one-line variant of the baseline composite?

investigations.name: mbp-01-time-varying-environment
investigations.objective:
Can v2ecoli's `media_update` / `exchange_data` Layer-1 Steps consume an
externally-driven, time-varying nutrient pool — instead of the static
media configuration baked into ParCa — such that metabolic exchange
fluxes and growth rate respond correctly to declining glucose, declining
DO, and other dynamic external concentrations?

investigations.name: mbp-02-population-aggregation
investigations.objective:
Can v2ecoli aggregate single-cell-plus-Division output into population-
level biomass observables (total gDW, cell count) that are physically
meaningful at the reactor scale (OD ≫ 1) — using a **representative-
sampling scaling factor (`cells_per_agent`)** so the simulated lineage
legitimately stands in for an N-cell population under the 0D
well-mixed assumption — and consume population-level signals (e.g.
reactor liquid volume) to maintain correct concentrations?

investigations.name: mbp-03-bird-reactor-coupling
investigations.objective:
Can v2ecoli (with the mbp-01 time-varying-env hook and mbp-02 population
aggregator) be coupled to `pbg-bioreactordesign`'s BiRDReactorProcess —
via a thin adapter that resolves the biomass-ownership conflict between
the two — such that BiRD supplies dissolved O2, kLa, gas-phase physics,
and v2ecoli supplies population biomass and exchange-flux demand,
producing a physically consistent coupled trajectory in a 0D
well-mixed bench-scale reactor?

investigations.name: mbp-04-multigeneration-runs
investigations.objective:
Does the mbp-03 coupled composite (v2ecoli ↔ pbg-bioreactordesign) stay
mass-conserving, computationally tractable, and physically coherent
over multiple v2ecoli generations (3+ doublings) under sustained
reactor dynamics — capturing the regime transition from glucose-replete
exponential growth into glucose-limited or DO-limited slowdown as the
population grows and consumes the batch?

investigations.name: mbp-05-palsson-benchmark
investigations.objective:
Configured with operating conditions matched to the 2025 Palsson lab
high-density E. coli study, does the v2ecoli ↔ pbg-bioreactordesign
coupled model **render a structured comparison report** (sim-vs-
published overlays + categorized divergences + open questions) on
the published WT batch-phase prefix trajectories, suitable to feed
mbp-06's gap-analysis synthesis?

Investigation-level note: the original question framing ("match within
tolerance") was reframed 2026-05-26 to "render a structured comparison."
The success definition is whether the comparison was EXECUTED AND
REPORTED COHERENTLY, not whether biology matched. All biological
divergences feed mbp-06 unchanged.

investigations.name: mbp-06-gap-analysis
investigations.objective:
After mbp-01..05 have produced their per-study findings, what are the
remaining gaps (in v2ecoli's biology coverage, the coupling layer, the
pbg-bioreactordesign physics, and the Beulig benchmark scope) that
prevent the investigation from answering its overarching question, and
how should those gaps be prioritized as the next investigation
iteration (mbp-* round 2, or a sibling investigation)?

investigations.name: mbp-07-millard-kinetic-metabolism
investigations.objective:
The Millard kinetic-metabolism arc, end-to-end. Can the Millard 2017
kinetic central-carbon ODE replace v2ecoli's constraint-based central-
carbon FBA as a drop-in cell engine under the cell-side interface
contract?

Three linked questions:
  1. BUILD     — does the swapped composite (baseline_millard) build and
                 run, with non-trivial live central fluxes (kinetic ODE
                 active, not FBA)?
  2. VALIDATE  — does the Millard whole-cell model recover growth
                 comparable to the FBA baseline, and (once the Millard
                 cell exposes mass-exchange accounting) close mass
                 conservation?
  3. COMPARE   — coupled to the same BiRD reactor and run against the
                 Beulig WT batch prefix, does the Millard kinetic central
                 metabolism track the bioreactor (growth, substrate, gas
                 transfer) BETTER than v2ecoli's WCM-FBA — and how do both
                 compare to the iML1515 genome-scale FBA (Palsson)?
                 Rendered as a structured 3-arm report-card comparison
                 (per-group axis verdicts + categorized divergences),
                 NOT a tolerance gate (execute-and-report, per
                 chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §10).

investigations.name: metabolism-biomass-yield-s1-diagnostic
investigations.title: Re-measure biomass yield on a recorded commit, and discriminate one defect from two
investigations.objective: On a fresh basal run whose code revision is recorded, what is the biomass yield - and does carbon close at the same time? The first half removes the provenance ambiguity in the committed fixtures; the second half is the discriminator, because if carbon closes at baseline while yield sits above the first-principles ceiling, the baseline defect is energetic and therefore distinct from the carbon creation seen under a binding uptake cap.

investigations.name: metabolism-biomass-yield-s1b-anaerobic-contrast
investigations.title: Does the model's own aerobic-to-anaerobic yield drop match biology?
investigations.objective: Real E. coli anaerobic biomass yield is several-fold below aerobic, because without a terminal electron acceptor the cell cannot extract ATP by respiration. A model that barely respires aerobically (O2:glucose ~0.09, RQ ~3.6) has little respiratory contribution to lose, so it should show a much smaller drop. Does it? This is a first-principles discriminator that needs no external reference data - the model is compared against its own aerobic result.

investigations.name: overflow-acetate-vs-growth
investigations.title: Does v2ecoli reproduce the aerobic acetate-overflow curve (acetate-carbon yield vs growth rate) — Vemuri 2006 / Basan 2015?
investigations.objective:
Across a glucose-uptake-rate titration, does v2ecoli reproduce the aerobic

investigations.name: param-uq-00-screen
investigations.title: Parameter screen — which config-reachable knobs actually drive the observables?
investigations.objective:
Among the top-level `ecoli-*` process-config scalars, which actually change the
growth observables when perturbed (so they're worth including in the UQ)?
investigations.claim:
Of the top-level process-config knobs reachable via `baseline()` config_overrides,
only 3 produce a real change in growth rate; the rest are inert.

investigations.name: param-uq-01-elongation
investigations.title: Ribosome basal elongation rate dominates growth-rate variance among effective elongation knobs (Sobol ≈ 0.97)
investigations.objective:
(1) Does the pbg-uq forward-UQ pipeline run end-to-end on v2ecoli? (2) Among the
elongation parameters that actually affect the simulation, which dominates
variance in instantaneous growth rate — and is the ranking robust across seeds?
investigations.claim:
Among the v2ecoli elongation knobs reachable via baseline config_overrides, the
ribosome's translation basal_elongation_rate ROBUSTLY DOMINATES variance in
instantaneous growth rate — total-order Sobol ≈ 0.97 (stable across 3 PCRV
seeds, range 0.955–0.987), vs ppGpp-synthesis kS ≈ 0.04 and DNA-pol elongation
rate ≈ 0.01. The PCE surrogate fits to ~1.7% test error. This CORRECTS the
initial demo, whose "gtpPerElongation dominates (0.88)" reading was a
state-carryover artifact (fixed in v2ecoli PR #197).

investigations.name: param-uq-02-observables
investigations.title: Multi-observable robustness — basal_elongation_rate dominates MASS; growth-rate ranking is window-dependent
investigations.objective:
Over a longer (360-step) window, do dry_mass and cell_mass become responsive to
the 3 effective elongation knobs, does basal_elongation_rate remain dominant
across observables, and is the ranking stable to the choice of observable/window?
investigations.claim:
Over a longer (360-step) window the MASS observables become responsive, and
basal_elongation_rate DOMINATES them — total-order Sobol ≈ 0.86 for both
dry_mass and cell_mass — confirming and extending the param-uq-01 finding to
mass. For instantaneous growth rate, however, the ranking is WINDOW-DEPENDENT:
ppGpp-synthesis kS edges basal_elongation_rate at 360 steps (0.62 vs 0.51), vs
basal's 0.97 at 120 steps. So the dominant driver of growth-rate variance shifts
with the integration window — a genuine nuance on top of the headline result.

investigations.name: pdmp-00-characterization
investigations.description:
Phase 0 of the v2ecoli → PDMP roadmap; its deliverables become the validation standard for every later
phase (a replacement subprocess is accepted when its interface statistics match the Phase 0 reference
Xarray dataset within tolerance). No biology is changed — v2ecoli runs as-is; the artefacts are the typed
interface schema library, the reference Xarray datasets across the ≥3 conditions, and the per-step
profiling report.

Conditions (tentative, spanning the metabolic regime the DUF report Sec. 4.1.1 notes has "approximately a
dozen"): aerobic M9 + glucose (canonical reference), M9 + acetate (slower growth, gluconeogenic flux), and
M9 + glucose + amino-acid mix (faster growth, partial relief on translation).

The reference datasets are ensembles, not single trajectories: N=64 independent stochastic replicates per
(condition, seed) put the standard error of the mean at σ/√N ≈ σ/8 = 12.5% of σ, enough to set a
Wasserstein-2 tolerance band without overfitting to MC noise; N is revisited after pilot N=8 batches and
raised per-observable if MCSE exceeds 10% of the inter-condition effect size. Per-step compute is profiled
as mean ± std over ≥1000 step samples (bootstrap 95% CI) into five buckets: FBA LP solve
(`wholecell.utils.modular_fba`, glpk-linear), RNG draws, store↔process marshalling, topology traversal, and
emitter I/O. Each categorized variable carries a numerical-sensitivity tier — Jacobian spectral-radius
contribution (ODE-amenable), per-step CV (stochastic-discrete), or coupling-strength L∞ norm
(coupling-artifact).

All runs use XArrayEmitter (workspace default; wired in the dashboard via PR #70); the reference dataset is
a zarr store per (condition, replicate, generation) opened downstream via xarray.open_zarr() with time-axis
chunking, and max_generations in workspace.yaml is set to 8 to cover the multi-generation lineage
statistics Phase 2 will consume.
investigations.title: Phase 0 — Characterization and Interface Extraction
investigations.objective: What is the Markov blanket of every major v2ecoli subprocess (metabolism, transcription, translation, replication, division, membrane), and how should every WCM state variable be categorized (ODE-amenable, stochastic discrete, teleonomic, or coupling artifact) so that subsequent phases have a typed interface contract to validate against?
investigations.claim:
Fixing per-process RNG seeding (crc32(process_name, master_seed)) makes multi-seed ensembles genuinely
diverge — v2ecoli's bare `seed` only seeded the allocator, so ensembles were bit-identical (confirmed on
an N=6 × 250 model-second M9-glucose pilot, .pbg/runs/phase0-traj/, ATP[c] CV ≈ 0.029%;
tests/test_seed_diversity.py passes). The canonical 192-run reference ensemble (3 conditions × N=64, 600 s)
is not committed in this checkout and is being re-run.

investigations.name: pdmp-01-metabolism-ode
investigations.description:
Phase 1 of the v2ecoli → PDMP roadmap: substitute v2ecoli's metabolism with the Millard 2017 kinetic ODE.

What v2ecoli's metabolism is: `v2ecoli/processes/metabolism.py` (`Metabolism` -> `FluxBalanceAnalysisModel`
-> `wholecell.utils.modular_fba.FluxBalanceAnalysis`, glpk-linear) solves one multi-objective FBA LP per
timestep combining (1) biomass production `max c^T v`; (2) homeostatic concentration targets toward
`conc_dict[media + doubling_time]` (optional ppGpp coupling when `include_ppgpp=True`); (3) kinetic-constraint
targets toward Vmax×[E] when `USE_KINETICS=True`. Constraints: `S v = 0`, enzyme-catalysis bounds, NGAM ATP
demand, media exchange bounds. Fluxes -> counts via `stochasticRound(flux × dry_mass × dt / (MW × conv))`;
the process runs LAST (deriver-style, post-partition). This differs structurally from textbook "tFBA"
(Birch, Udell & Covert 2014), a sequence of target-tracking LPs.

What blocks likelihood-based inference: the stochasticRound LP->counts map is non-smooth and RNG-dependent;
enzyme-bound changes make consecutive LP solutions jump between polytope vertices; GLPK returns an arbitrary
vertex of a degenerate optimum facet; doubling-time is both input (homeostatic targets) and output (biomass
rate) without a separated equation; and the kinetic-constraint terms re-read enzyme abundances each step, so
the LP is non-autonomous in a way tied to the discrete-time loop.

Substitution target: Millard et al. 2017 ([[millard2017]]), a curated kinetic ODE of E. coli central carbon
+ energy metabolism (glycolysis/EMP, gluconeogenesis, PPP, Entner-Doudoroff, anaplerotic, TCA, glyoxylate
shunt, acetate, nucleotide interconversion, oxidative phosphorylation), calibrated for K-12 MG1655 on
M9 + glucose at dilution rate 0.1 h⁻¹, pH 7.0, 37 °C, pO₂ > 20%; calibration to acetate / glucose+aa is part
of this study. Rather than re-derive the rate laws, we wrap the published SBML (BioModels MODEL1505110000)
with pbg-copasi (https://github.com/vivarium-collective/pbg-copasi) as a `CopasiUTCProcess` /
`CopasiSteadyStateStep` over the COPASI/basico backend, keeping the SBML as source of truth.

FBA-bridge composite: because Phase 1 cannot rip out the multi-objective FBA at once (the rest of v2ecoli
reads its flux outputs, and its homeostatic + kinetic-constraint terms couple to translation/transcription
we are not touching), the ODE and FBA run side by side — the ODE drives central-carbon flux (the Millard
network) while the FBA covers the rest (non-central homeostatic targets, out-of-scope enzyme-catalysed
reactions, NGAM). The bridge schema is the contract; once it holds interface fidelity across all Phase 0
conditions the seam moves outward in later studies. The LQR layer replaces the FBA biomass-production
objective with a parameterised growth-rate controller (risk: the reference trajectory reintroducing a
teleonomic parameter in disguise).

Numerical: COPASI/basico defaults to LSODA (adaptive stiff/non-stiff, for the stiffness between sub-second
pool equilibration and >10² s growth dynamics) at rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-9 (one order tighter than defaults) so
solution error stays below the Phase 0 MC noise floor ([[uq-bootstrap-cis-on-interface-stats]]); a Richardson
step-doubling check confirms solver order before LQR tuning. Acceptance uses W₂(p_ODE, p_ref) per interface
variable within the Phase 0 bootstrap CI of the self-MC W₂ spread. Before Phase 3, causal parameters pass FIM
conditioning (κ(FIM) < 10⁸) + profile-likelihood width; LQR weights pass Sobol (first-order + total), and
weights the system is insensitive to are removed. All runs use XArrayEmitter conforming to the Phase 0
schema, compared via xarray.open_zarr(..., chunks={'time': -1, 'replicate': 1}).
investigations.title: Phase 1 — Metabolism: multi-objective FBA → Kinetic ODE
investigations.objective:
Can the Millard et al. 2017 kinetic ODE of E. coli central carbon
and energy metabolism, wrapped in a linear-quadratic regulator
(LQR) outer control layer for growth-rate regulation, replace
v2ecoli's multi-objective FBA metabolism (biomass + homeostatic +
kinetic-constraint, via `wholecell.utils.modular_fba`) while
reproducing the Phase 0 interface statistics within tolerance
across ≥3 environmental conditions?
investigations.claim:
On M9-glucose the PDMP metabolism (Millard 2017 kinetic ODE via pbg-copasi + consumption_matched driver with
the closed-loop WATER[c] fix, commit 6a764fc) meets the ±σ W₂ acceptance gate against the N=32 Phase-0
ensemble: cell_mass W₂/σ = 1.00, dry_mass W₂/σ = 1.09 (N=12 replicates, seeds 1000–1011). The FBA-bridge
flux-pin integrates the kinetic ODE into the WCM FBA (24 active pins) so glycolysis + pentose-phosphate hold
exactly while the TCA relaxes (growth-coupled); the multi-condition (acetate / +aa) W₂ and the LQR Sobol/FIM
audit remain pending.

investigations.name: pdmp-02-jump-processes
investigations.description:
Phase 2 of the v2ecoli → PDMP roadmap. The discrete-time layer is the most numerically suspect part of
v2ecoli: stochastic-draw parametrization depends on the ratio of the fixed timestep to the teleonomic
"doubling time" (DUF Sec. 4.1.1), and the global reallocation step exists to paper over
mass-conservation violations from composing independent processes (DUF Sec. 2.1). A PDMP formulation
has neither: events occur at random times from explicit propensity functions, division is a
first-passage time of a continuous observable, and resource competition is state-dependent jump
kernels. The contract to verify is that between any two jumps the state evolves deterministically under
the coupled ODE, with jumps at times set by ∫ λ(s) ds = E for E ~ Exp(1).

# Numerical considerations
Stochastic integration. Gillespie SSA is exact but slow at single-cell mRNA/protein propensity scales
(10²–10⁴ events / s). The per-process choice (exact SSA vs. τ-leaping vs. hybrid) trades variance
against compute: ribosome-elongation uses τ-leaping with τ set so the leap condition (Δλ/λ < 0.03)
holds; rare promoter firing uses exact next-reaction.

Exponential-clock validation. The core correctness test is that the cumulative hazard ∫ λ(s) ds at
successive events is Exp(1)-distributed — an Anderson-Darling test over ≥10⁴ inter-event intervals per
jump process (α = 0.05). A failed test indicates a propensity bug.

First-passage validation. Division is a first-passage time for volume crossing a threshold. Before the
full WCM we validate the integrator on an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with exact Bessel-function FPT:
the empirical FPT must match the analytical CDF to KS distance < 0.02 over N=10⁴ trajectories.

Distribution-match resolution. Trajectory ensembles vs. baseline are compared with W₂ on summary
statistics (growth rate, mean per-gene mRNA/protein, division-time CV). N=200 PDMP trajectories per
condition gives W₂ MCSE ≈ σ_W₂/√200 ≈ 0.07 σ_W₂ — enough to detect deviations of ≥0.2 σ; sample size
is revisited if MCSE > 10% of the inter-baseline effect size.

PDMP integrator validity. The Markov property is tested by re-simulating segments with the same
(state, RNG seed) and confirming bit-identical determinism between jumps.

# Emitter
XArrayEmitter records each jump event as a row in a separate zarr group ('jumps') alongside the
continuous trajectory group ('continuous'). max_generations=8 in workspace.yaml accommodates the
multi-generation division-time CV / mother-daughter inheritance distributions compared to baseline.
investigations.title: Phase 2 — Jump Process Layer: Discrete-Time → Continuous-Time Stochastic
investigations.objective:
Can v2ecoli's discrete-time stochastic layer (Poisson gene-expression draws scaled by
timestep/doubling time, the teleonomic division trigger, and the globally-acting resource
reallocation correction) be replaced by a coherent continuous-time jump process that, coupled with
the Phase 1 metabolism ODE, satisfies the Markov property of a piecewise-deterministic Markov process?
investigations.claim:
The `pdmp-trajectory-distribution-match` gate FAILED on cell_mass: the Poisson tau-leap Wasserstein-2
grows monotonically 9.73 → 15.35 → 49.46. This is a legitimate negative result — cell_mass is the
wrong observable because the consumption_matched homeostat washes per-tick variance out, so Phase-3
inference must anchor on count-level listeners, not mass.

investigations.name: pdmp-03-inference
investigations.description:
Phase 3 of the v2ecoli → PDMP roadmap. With the PDMP in place, every trajectory is a sample from a
well-defined process measure with a constructible likelihood; this phase makes that likelihood
computable and tractable for Bayesian workflows. ChiRho (BasisResearch, 2024) is the reference for the
algebraic-effect interpretation of observe / intervene, and the DUF report Sec. 4.2.2 notes Vivarium
can be read as a domain-specific algebraic effect system for discrete-event simulation. ABC-SMC is the
baseline engine because it is robust to nonlinear, partially observed dynamics; the structured-
population layer handles the fact that omics data are bulk-culture expectations over the single-cell
PDMP measure.

# Numerical considerations
Likelihood library. Each modality's likelihood is fit with its dispersion/noise scale and reported with
a 95% CI: RNA-seq NegBin(μ, φ), φ MLE'd on held-out calibration (expect φ ∈ [0.1, 1.0] for E. coli);
proteomics LogNormal(μ, σ²), σ from technical-replicate spread (σ_log ≈ 0.2 for SILAC/iBAQ); growth
Normal(log μ, σ_μ²) on log-scale; metabolomics Normal/LogNormal per-metabolite by dynamic range.

Accumulator numerics. Log-likelihood contributions are summed in log space to avoid underflow (typical
full-run log-likelihood ≪ -10³); mixtures use log-sum-exp with the shift trick; cross-cell population
reductions use pairwise/Kahan summation so the result is order-independent and reproducible.

ABC-SMC schedule. ε-decay is adaptive at quantile q=0.5 of the previous population's distance, minimum
population N=1000, terminating on ESS < 0.5·N or a wall-clock cap. Distance (PLANNED, NOT YET
IMPLEMENTED — the current pilot uses an unweighted SSE/Euclidean distance with no covariance and no
condition-number/kappa guard): Mahalanobis on a hand-picked summary vector (growth rate, mean log-mRNA
and log-protein per high-coverage gene, key metabolite log-conc). Posterior ESS and acceptance rate are
reported every SMC step.

Posterior calibration. Simulation-Based Calibration (Talts et al. 2018): for K=1000 draws of (θ*, y*),
run ABC-SMC and record the rank of θ*; the rank histogram must pass a χ² uniformity test (p > 0.05) and
90% credible intervals must reach ≥85% empirical coverage. K=1000 gives rank-resolution 1/(K+1) ≈ 10⁻³.

Identifiability. Re-run the Phase 1 Fisher-information check for any new parameters (likelihood
dispersions, population-layer parameters) and flag non-identifiable combinations.

# Emitter
ABC-SMC iterates ~10⁶ PDMP runs, so XArrayEmitter runs in "summary-only" mode writing only the
predeclared summary-statistic vector per trajectory (zarr group 'summary'), skipping full time-series.
Posterior particles, per-SMC-step ε, ESS, and acceptance go to zarr ('posterior'/'diagnostics'); SBC
runs (K=1000) produce a separate zarr keyed by SBC iteration for rank-histogram analysis.
investigations.title: Phase 3 — Inference Infrastructure: Likelihoods and Bayesian Interface
investigations.objective:
Can the Phase 2 PDMP support well-formed observation likelihoods for the dominant cell-biology
measurement modalities (RNA-seq, proteomics, growth rate, metabolomics) and recover posteriors via
ABC-SMC on synthetic data — establishing the inference-ready substrate that motivated the DUF rescoping?
investigations.claim:
A likelihood → emission → XArrayEmitter(zarr) → rejection-ABC pipeline runs on a self-generated toy
parameter grid. On a 3×3 (Ts, Ps) grid (N=4 replicates, 60 s) the combined count vector
sqrt(d_rna² + d_ribosome²) separates truth from its next-nearest cell better (3.06×) than aggregate
log-likelihood (2.39×) — a grid-separation diagnostic, not a posterior or credible interval.

investigations.name: pdmp-04-compilation
investigations.description:
Phase 4 of the v2ecoli → PDMP roadmap. The DUF report Sec. 4.2.1 notes that "submodel definitions and
simulation modules are currently inseparable" in v2ecoli and that the runtime "exhibits orders of
magnitude of overhead, relative to competitive numerical solvers" — the dominant cause being
marshalling overhead from the row-centric nested-dictionary state. Catalyst.jl + ModelingToolkit +
JumpProcesses.jl is the reference target: an established Julia stack for compiled reaction-network
simulation with symbolic Jacobians and GPU-friendly state. The PB → Catalyst.jl bridge — codifying the
PB process interface as a Catalyst-compatible reaction-network spec — is the primary new deliverable;
the column-centric refactor of Vivarium can proceed in parallel with Phases 1–2.

# Numerical considerations
Numerical equivalence. The hardest test is whether the compiled runner produces the same trajectory
ensemble as the Phase 2 runner: W₂(p_compiled, p_phase2) ≤ 5·σ_MC, where σ_MC is the standard error of
the Phase 2 self-W₂ at the same N (5σ is conservative — it covers genuine FP-order differences without
firing on stochastic noise). Tested on N=10⁴ trajectories across all Phase 0 conditions.

Precision. FP32 on GPU promises 2× throughput but corrupts long-run ABC posteriors via catastrophic
cancellation in propensity sums. Default FP64; FP32 only where (a) bit-equivalence vs FP64 passes and
(b) downstream ABC posteriors are invariant under the switch.

FP summation order. Parallel reductions over per-trajectory log-likelihoods must use deterministic
(pairwise or Kahan) summation so results are independent of GPU thread scheduling; non-deterministic
atomic-add reductions are banned (they break SBC reproducibility across hardware).

Convergence orders. ODE: order-5 embedded Runge-Kutta (default) or BDF for stiff segments, verified on
Van der Pol + Brusselator before deployment. SSA jumps: exact. τ-leaping: weak order 1, strong order
0.5, tested on the analytical M/M/1 queue.

Throughput vs variance. The relevant metric is posterior-estimate-variance per wall-clock second, not
raw trajectories/second; we report both trajectories/sec at fixed precision and ABC posterior variance
× wall-clock time. Doubling trajectories should roughly halve posterior variance (1/√N); if not, the
parallelism has hidden correlations to investigate.

# Emitter
Compiled-runner output goes through a Julia → XArrayEmitter bridge that batches per-trajectory results
into chunked zarr writes (chunks: {trajectory: 64, time: -1}) at the python boundary, avoiding
per-trajectory I/O at 10³+ parallelism. The bridge preserves bit-equivalence with the Phase 2 emitter
so the W₂ equivalence test [[uq-compiled-vs-reference-w2-5sigma]] can compare paired zarr stores.
investigations.title: Phase 4 — Compilation and Performance
investigations.objective:
Can the Phase 2 PDMP be exported to a high-performance compiled representation (Catalyst.jl /
ModelingToolkit with symbolic Jacobians and automatic sensitivity equations) on a column-centric
Vivarium runtime, achieving ≥10³ parallel single-cell trajectories on a GPU or multi-core CPU with
near-zero per-step marshalling overhead — turning the throughput bottleneck the DUF report identified
into a non-issue for downstream inference?
investigations.claim:
Profiling shows ~76% of per-tick time is spent outside process_update, but that bucket includes real
numpy/scipy numeric work (e.g. Poisson logpmf), so it is not all marshalling overhead. The headline
"total speedup at N=10³" is an illustrative projection (a hand-picked toy factor × N), not a measurement
— the column-centric vectorized runtime was never built or timed, only the pbg side was measured (at
N=1,2,4), and the per-Process Catalyst.jl JIT ≤10% figure is an unvalidated extrapolation.

investigations.name: pdmp-05-causal-discovery
investigations.description:
Phase 5 of the v2ecoli → PDMP roadmap and the final phase, pursuing the DUF ARC goal of
simulation-based causal discovery in WCMs. It depends on every preceding phase: the PDMP for process
likelihoods (Phase 2), the observation-likelihood library and accumulator (Phase 3), and the compiled
high-throughput runtime that makes marginal-likelihood estimation feasible (Phase 4). Each candidate
gene-function annotation defines a different WCM; we marginalize over parameters and compare via
marginal likelihoods, with Russian Roulette estimators (Lyne et al. 2015) giving unbiased estimates of
the otherwise intractable marginals. Active causal inference (Toth et al. 2022) runs the experiment-
design loop, proposing interventions whose outcomes most sharply distinguish competing annotations. The
benchmark set holds ≥20 E. coli genes with literature-established functions across diverse mechanism
classes (kinases, transcription factors, transporters, structural proteins).

# Numerical considerations
Marginal likelihood numerics. Russian Roulette (Lyne et al. 2015) gives unbiased estimators of
intractable normalizing constants Z = ∫ p(D|θ) p(θ) dθ via a truncated geometric series with importance
weights. The estimator can have unbounded variance, so we monitor empirical variance over batches and
require an ESS-equivalent N_eff ≥ 100 per Z estimate; below that the result is flagged and we use a
tighter proposal or fall back to thermodynamic integration / nested sampling with documented bias.

Bayes factor confidence intervals. Report log Bayes factors with a 95% bootstrap CI from the RR
variance bound, not point estimates. Conclusions fire only if the CI sits entirely above the
Jeffreys-scale threshold (|log BF| > 1, "substantial evidence").

SBC at the model-comparison level. Extend SBC to model comparison: for K=500 synthetic datasets each
generated under a known true annotation, the recovered posterior model probability should be uniform
conditional on the true model index (Talts et al. 2018, Cook et al. 2006). A non-uniform rank histogram
signals miscalibration before we trust it on novel annotations.

Active inference numerics. Expected information gain (EIG) is estimated via nested Monte Carlo (outer
over experiments, inner over (θ, y) pairs). Standard NMC has bias O(1/N_inner), so we use
Donsker-Varadhan or DAD-MINE variational lower bounds where feasible, else NMC with explicit bias
bounds. Every intervention proposal carries its EIG ± MCSE; the loop never selects an intervention whose
EIG CI overlaps zero.

False discovery control. Benchmark recoveries report per-annotation posterior probability and a
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at the gene-set level; a q-value ≤ 0.1 is required before declaring a benchmark
recovery successful.

Convergence rate of credible-interval widths. Report the shrinkage rate: sub-√n is the standard MCMC
rate (posterior-mean variance ∝ 1/n_eff_samples); slower than n^{-1/2} indicates poor mixing or
non-identifiability and triggers diagnosis.

# Emitter
Each candidate-annotation run writes a zarr store with (a) the RR marginal-likelihood estimator
trajectory, (b) the per-annotation posterior, and (c) the intervention-selection record + EIG
estimates. The benchmark gene-set sweep aggregates per-gene zarr stores into one zarr group per
benchmark, readable via xarray.open_mfdataset() for the gene-set-level BH-FDR summary.
investigations.title: Phase 5 — Causal Discovery and Functional Annotation
investigations.objective:
Can the compiled, likelihood-equipped PDMP WCM support Bayesian model comparison for gene-function
annotation — recovering known E. coli gene functions on a benchmark set with credible intervals that
shrink with sample size, and driving an active causal-inference loop that selects in-silico
interventions to maximally discriminate between candidate mechanisms?
investigations.claim:
At ±15% hypothesis spacing the unbiased pseudo-marginal posterior is essentially uniform (log BF
+0.01, truth 24.4% vs 20% baseline) and replicate count cannot rescue it (kernel-mean gap Δlog +0.011
sets an information-theoretic ceiling). Wider spacing lifts truth posterior to 61% but log BF tops out
at +0.45 (< Jeffreys substantial), so the single remaining lever in the current design space is
observable choice.

investigations.name: population_phenotype_basal
investigations.title: Basal-condition physiology — v2ecoli baseline vs experimental literature
investigations.objective:
Does the v2ecoli baseline single-cell→division ensemble reproduce the
basal-condition physiology of glucose-minimal MG1655 — growth rate, biomass
yield, glucose uptake, central-carbon fluxes, exchange rates, proteome census,
macromolecular composition, and metabolite pools — when graded against curated
experimental + theoretical reference values rather than a pinned run?

investigations.name: s01-birth-and-division
investigations.objective:
Pack the simulated whole-cell molecular state into a 3D cell at ~10 s
(post-equilibration birth) and right before division, so the Parsimony Viewer
can show both declared-time snapshots for this study.

investigations.name: showcase-1-parca
investigations.title: Rebuild the ParCa in full from the ecoli-sources flat files
investigations.objective:
Can v2ecoli rebuild the ParCa in full from the ~133 ecoli-sources flat
files? Running the ParCa pipeline with --mode full should fit all 51 TF
conditions (the full-mode proof, vs ~7 in fast/debug mode) and emit a
complete cache bundle (initial_state.json + sim_data_cache.dill + metadata +
cache_version) that reproduces the parca_compare reference.

investigations.name: showcase-2-baseline-figures
investigations.title: Wild-type baseline single-cell→division ensemble reproduces E. coli properties
investigations.objective:
Does the baseline single-cell→division sim reproduce wild-type E. coli
properties across a multiseed/multigen ensemble? The wild-type baseline
resumed from the showcase-1 full ParCa cache should produce a doubling time
in band, physiological mass fractions, FBA fluxes that correlate with Toya
2010, and a proteome that correlates with Schmidt 2016 / Wisniewski.

investigations.name: showcase-3-variant-decide
investigations.title: Which perturbation best demonstrates v2ecoli's response — reviewers to choose
investigations.objective:
Which perturbation best demonstrates v2ecoli's response — reviewers to
choose? Building on the wild-type baseline (showcase-2), this study stops at
a DECISION: it commits no variant. Four candidate perturbations are proposed;
reviewers pick which one (or more) best demonstrates v2ecoli's perturbation
response. No simulation runs until a variant is chosen.

investigations.name: showcase-4-variant-comparison
investigations.title: Five-variant perturbation sweep — which perturbation most clearly moves v2ecoli off baseline
investigations.objective:
Of the four perturbations proposed in showcase-3 (ppGpp regulation OFF, a
dnaA 2x expression knob, a slower ribosome elongation rate, and a media /
condition change to succinate), which one most clearly and interpretably
moves the v2ecoli whole cell off its wild-type baseline? Run all four as a
single multivariant sweep against the showcase-2 baseline and quantify each
variant's delta across growth, replication, regulation, central-carbon flux,
and proteome.

investigations.name: showcase-5-next-direction-decide
investigations.title: Which direction next — deepen the strongest perturbation contrast (reviewers to choose)
investigations.objective:
Given the showcase-4 5-variant sweep, which direction should the showcase
take next? The sweep produced a clear ranking — media / growth-condition
change was the strongest, most interpretable contrast; the ppGpp-off
de-repression was the most informative surprise; elong-down was a near-null.
This study stops at a DECISION: it commits no variant. Candidate next
directions are seeded from those results; reviewers pick which one (or more)
to pursue. No simulation runs until a direction is chosen.

investigations.name: showcase-6-equivalence-large
investigations.title: v1↔v2 equivalence at scale: a large (16×16) baseline ensemble graded against vEcoli
investigations.objective:
Is the v2ecoli wild-type baseline still "the same E. coli" as vEcoli (v1) when
measured at LARGE ensemble scale? This study applies the PR #134 behavioral
report-card approach (population_phenotype_basal in its v1↔v2 *equivalence*
reference mode) to a large multi-generation baseline ensemble — 16 seeds × 16
generations — and grades v2's emergent population phenotype against a matched
vEcoli 16×16 reference within tolerance. #134 exercised the same loop at 8×16
as a demo; this study scales it to a population large enough to tighten the
omics/flux equivalence axes and to read v2's multi-generation behavior (the
in-process sawtooth, #142) honestly against v1.

investigations.name: sm-00-data-collection
investigations.title: Surrogate data collection — broad observable transition-dataset from baseline rollouts
investigations.objective:
Can the deeply-nested baseline state (pint Quantities, per-agent keys,
dict-valued exchange fluxes, high-dimensional count/flux vectors) be extracted
into a stable, flat (state_t, state_t+1) transition dataset covering every
observable category?
investigations.claim:
An 8-seed ensemble of baseline rollouts can be flattened into a single
pbg-torch TransitionDataset spanning a broad observable panel (growth/mass,
exchange fluxes, metabolic fluxes, protein and transcript abundance,
chromosome state) — ~11.5k observables per step — suitable for training a
neural-network surrogate.

investigations.name: sm-01-nn-surrogate
investigations.title: NN surrogate — does it beat trivial baselines?
investigations.objective:
Does the neural-network surrogate beat trivial baselines (persistence,
mean-delta, linear) on the baseline's per-step dynamics — and are the
high-dimensional observables learnable from the observable view at all?
investigations.claim:
Tested honestly against trivial baselines under cross-validation, the neural
surrogate does NOT beat them: one-step R²≈1.0 is a persistence artifact (the
signal is smooth), and in multi-step rollout a LINEAR model is the best and
most stable emulator of coarse growth/mass while the neural net matches it at
best and destabilizes on 2/8 folds. The broad ~11.5k-observable panel is not
learnable from the observable view alone (0% of observables beat persistence).
A neural surrogate is not justified for these targets on this evidence.

investigations.name: sm-02-utility-and-limits
investigations.title: Utility & limits — what a cheap emulator buys, and where emulation ends
investigations.objective:
Given that the linear emulator (not the neural net) is the model that works
for coarse growth, is it actually worth building — i.e. does it amortize
against the cost of generating its training data — and what are its limits?
investigations.claim:
The honest by-product of sm-01 — a cheap LINEAR emulator of coarse growth —
is genuinely useful: it pays back its 8 training simulations after ~8
evaluations and sweeps 5,000 trajectories in 0.02 s (vs ~24 h on the WCM,
~3.8e6× per trajectory). Its limits are explicit: it emulates a smooth,
low-dimensional observable view, not the cell's high-dimensional hidden state.

investigations.name: sm-03-improving-the-surrogate
investigations.title: Improving the surrogate — does rollout-loss training close the gap?
investigations.objective:
sm-01 diagnosed the neural net's weakness as autoregressive instability from
one-step training. Does the principled fix — multi-step rollout-loss training —
close the gap to the linear baseline?
investigations.claim:
Multi-step rollout-loss training (the net trains on its own unrolled
predictions) genuinely improves the neural surrogate — it eliminates the
autoregressive instability (0/8 unstable folds vs 1/8 for one-step training)
and lowers rollout error (median nRMSE 0.053 vs 0.069). It still does not beat
the linear baseline (0.019) for this smooth target, but it is the right
technique to carry to harder, genuinely nonlinear targets.

investigations.name: sm-04-through-division
investigations.title: Through division — do the emulators hold across the cell-cycle discontinuity?
investigations.objective:
Do the linear and neural (rollout-loss) emulators of coarse growth, which
emulate a single generation well (sm-01/sm-03), continue to hold when a
trajectory crosses a division event where cell_mass halves and the chromosome
count resets — or is the cell-cycle discontinuity a hard boundary the
observable-view emulator cannot represent?
investigations.claim:
The load-bearing untested boundary of the whole investigation: every sm-0x
conclusion is conditioned on pre-division single-cell trajectories, because
sm-00 halts each rollout at division ("the single-agent assumption breaks once
daughters appear"). sm-04 extends collection to follow ONE daughter lineage
across a real division event and finds that the emulators which win within a
generation (linear best; the sm-03 rollout-loss NN) do NOT hold across it:
none represents the cell_mass halving. This is an informative negative that
scopes the emulator to within-generation validity.
